minutes.headline: Board reviewed special Town Meeting articles; sewer service extension for one Cross Street property left unresolved
minutes.summary: The board approved a Salvation Army boot drive permit, heard the town manager's report, and went through the articles for the special Town Meeting the following week. The board also edited the old primary school reuse survey and then entered executive session on the police union contract.

what_happened.line: The Select Board reviewed special Town Meeting articles and made no recommendation on extending the sewer service area for a Cross Street property.
The board passed a permit for a Salvation Army boot drive on December 14th at two locations.
Members agreed edits to the old primary school reuse survey, including new/renovation labels and changing "modernize" to "renovate".
Members agreed Mr. Jeffries will present article 13, the old primary non-binding resolution, and asked staff for a rough annual per-road-mile plowing and sanding estimate.
The board entered executive session on the police union contract at the close of the meeting.

why_it_matters: A sewer service area extension can make land easier to develop, which can add homes, traffic and sewer demand, so the article is one residents may be asked to vote on at the special Town Meeting.
New roads the town accepts bring ongoing plowing, drain and resurfacing costs that fall on the town budget, mostly taxes, and the board asked for a per-mile estimate to size them.
watch_next: The special Town Meeting the following week, where the sewer service article and article 13 on the old primary school come up.
The 6:00 pre-meeting, where town counsel is to be consulted on the sewer service article.
